records.verbatim_quote: p.25: "The type of H_alpha({5,3,3}) is {30/(1,11),3}, and for alpha = 0 no vertices identify, so that H_0({5,3,3}) can be taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope, but not H_1({5,3,3}) in which four vertices come together." p.23: "The general H_alpha({4,3,3}) has type {8/(1,3),3}. In this case, for alpha = 0 no vertices come together, so we still have a chiral polyhedron H_0({4,3,3}), which was taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope in S3 (or R4) in [3]. See Figure 6." p.26 Fig. 8: "The part of H_0({5,3,3}) that touches the (central) dodecahedral facet of {5,3,3}, and an outside view of it with a face highlighted in red." p.31: "The interested reader can find the source code for computing the matrices for each of the polyhedra, together with more pictures of them in the website https://www.matem.unam.mx/~roli/PetrieCoxeter.html" (braces reconstructed from PyPDF2 output).

In preparation.' and [31] Hubard–Trejo 'A family of skeletal chiral 3- and 4-polytopes in R^4. Preprint'.

records.title: IN109023 Informe Final 2023 — 'Poliedros esqueléticos altamente simétricos en espacios de dimensión 3 y 4' (PAPIIT grant final report; NOT a citer of (A), but documents the unpublished follow-up work)
records.authors: Responsable: Isabel Alicia Hubard Escalera (Instituto de Matemáticas, UNAM); participants named include Javier Bracho, Briseida Trejo, Ernesto Vázquez, [D.] González Casanova
records.venue: DGAPA-UNAM PAPIIT transparency report, 12 pages, 'Fecha de actualización: 02/07/2025'
records.how_found: Web search for González-Casanova UNAM thesis; PDF fetched and text-extracted with PyPDF2.
records.relevance: Directly on the research question: reports (i) Trejo–Hubard's classification of chiral skeletal polyhedra whose 1-skeleton lies in the graph of a regular convex 4-polytope ('únicamente 4 ejemplos') and the determination of which of them extend to chiral 4-polytopes in E^4 (article 'que se someterá a publicación próximamente'), and (ii) González Casanova's construction with Hubard and Bracho of 'un par de nuevos 4-politpos quirales' from regular starry 4-polytopes (= item (C)). The report does not mention Pellicer, Petrie-Coxeter, or the paper (A) by name; the 'PRODUCTIVIDAD' list contains no publication on these 4-polytopes.
records.verbatim_quote: "clasificar los poliedros esqueléticos quirales cuyo 1-esqueleto está contenido en la gráfica de un 4-politopo convexo regular. La estudiante Trejo, con apoyo de la Dra. Hubard, logró dar dicha clasificación, obteniendo únicamente 4 ejemplos." ... "una de las metas del proyecto fue la de usar los poliedros esqueléticos quirales cuyo 1-esqueleto está contenido en la gráfica de un 4-politopo convexo regular para construir 4-politopos quirales en el espacio euclidiano de 4 dimensiones. Este trabajo tuvo buenos resultados: de los 4 poliedros quirales que existen ..., se determinaron cuáles de ellos se pueden extender." ... "el estudiante González Casanova trabajó con la Dra. Hubard y el Dr. Bracho en construir un par de nuevos 4-politpos quirales en el espacio de 4 dimensiones. Para esto, estudió a profundidad algunos 4-politopos estrellados regulares de dicho espacio y les aplicó una serie de operaciones para obtener poliedros quirales. Después, logró encontrar isometrías que lo han ayudado a extender los poliedros a 4-politopos quirales."
records.confidence: high (text retrieved verbatim); relevance to (A) inferred from subject matter, not from an explicit citation

notes: SUMMARY. Across Semantic Scholar (DOI endpoint), Google Scholar, zbMATH Open (rf: reverse query), Crossref, OpenAlex and OpenCitations, exactly TWO works citing paper (A) were found as of 2026-09-07: (1) Hubard & Schulte, 'Two-Orbit Polytopes', arXiv:2604.00185 (31 Mar 2026) — cites (A) once in a survey sentence and says nothing about H_alpha(T) or facets; (2) Pellicer, 'A chiral 5-polytope of full rank', Discrete Math. 344 (2021) 112370 — cites (A) as 'accepted for publication'; citing passage not retrieved (paywalled, no OA copy). No index lists any work that constructs a chiral 4-polytope with an H_alpha(T) facet beyond Roli's cube itself (H_0({4,3,3}) facet, per (A) p.23). The Bracho–González-Casanova–Hubard manuscript (item (C)) is documented only as 'In preparation' (ref. [1] of arXiv:2604.00185) and narratively in the PAPIIT IN109023 final report; no public copy, thesis record, or arXiv id was found — this is 'not found', not evidence of non-existence. A second unpublished item directly on the research question surfaced: Hubard & Trejo, 'A family of skeletal chiral 3- and 4-polytopes in R^4' (ref. [31] 'Preprint' in arXiv:2604.00185; the IN109023 report describes it as extending some of the 4 chiral polyhedra whose 1-skeleton lies in the graph of a regular convex 4-polytope to chiral 4-polytopes in E^4). Pellicer's 2025 CUP monograph 'Abstract Chiral Polytopes' (Ch. 6 'Skeletal Polytopes') could not be checked (HTTP 429) and remains a possible unverified citer.
